symptom: CORRECTED 2026-08-18 after testing the original diagnosis and finding it wrong. The original text claimed confirm.py rejects any uppercase gate path outright. Case-folding is correct for matching an oracle NAME against the deterministic allowlist; it is wrong for a path. This is masked on Windows because NTFS is case-insensitive, and would break on any case-sensitive filesystem -- i.e. Linux CI -- where every gate in this project (all uppercase F-NNNN names) would report 'no such gate is on disk (F-0023)'. Latent, not active here.

The properties class defaults the secret to an empty string and application.yml has no placeholder for it at all under the shopify block, so a deploy that never sets the property boots cleanly and then silently rejects every Shopify webhook as unsigned — order tracking and coupon redemptions stop with no loud failure anywhere.
missed_by: No startup config assertion for the Shopify webhook secret, and no smoke test posting a signed webhook against a deployed environment.

symptom: [Shopify Integration / medium Q19] The Shopify connect controller exposes only authorize and callback, and the revoke method on the token storage has no caller anywhere in the application. There is no API path by which a brand can disconnect a Shopify store, so a connection can be created but never removed through the product.
missed_by: No endpoint-coverage check that every storage mutation, including revoke, is reachable from a route.

symptom: [Shopify Integration / medium Q19] Reconnecting Shopify without disconnecting takes the existing-row branch, which rotates the access token and scopes in place but never rewrites shop_domain. A brand that points the same workspace at a different store ends up with a row still keyed to the first store's domain while holding the second store's token, so webhook lookups by shop domain resolve to the wrong store.
missed_by: No test reconnects a workspace to a different shop domain and asserts the persisted domain.

symptom: [WooCommerce Integration / medium Q23] Connect resolves the existing WooCommerce row by workspace and the rotate method replaces only the encrypted secret, never site_url. A brand that reconnects pointing at a different site keeps the original site_url on the row while holding the new site's secret: webhooks from the new site 404 on lookup, and webhooks from the old site verify against the wrong secret and 401. Conversion tracking for that brand goes silently dead in both directions.
missed_by: No test reconnects a workspace to a different site URL and then posts a webhook from it.

symptom: [WooCommerce Integration / high Q25] The webhook idempotency key hashes site URL, topic and order id, and both order.created and order.updated are in the acted-on topic set. The same order delivered under both topics yields two different keys, passes both reservation layers and writes two coupon_redemptions rows with two coupon usage increments for a single purchase. The database unique constraint is on the idempotency key alone, not on coupon plus order, so it does not catch it either. Shopify has the identical shape with orders/create and orders/paid.
missed_by: Idempotency tests replay the same topic twice; none deliver the same order under two different acted-on topics.

symptom: [Conversion Tracking (Generic + UTM) / medium Q27] Calling the generate endpoint a second time rotates the conversion webhook secret in place rather than adding a row, and the plaintext is revealed only in that one response. Any signature the brand's system was already producing becomes invalid immediately, with no warning on the generate call and no way to read the previous secret back.
missed_by: No test or UX check covers regenerating a secret while an integration is live.

symptom: [Conversion Tracking (Generic + UTM) / high Q29] The conversion reservation key is built from workspace id, a literal separator, the UTM id and the order id; the caller-supplied idempotency key plays no part in the dedup decision and is only forwarded to the audit row. Two genuinely distinct conversions on the same UTM link that happen to share an order id are silently collapsed into one, and a caller that varies the order id can double-count the same sale no matter what idempotency key it sends. Revenue and conversion counts on utm_campaigns are wrong in both directions.
missed_by: Idempotency tests vary the supplied key only; none vary the order id while holding the key fixed, or repeat an order id across distinct sales.

symptom: [Conversion Tracking (Generic + UTM) / medium Q16, 30, 43] The redemption write path saves the redemption row, bumps the coupon usage count and records a money audit event, but never calls the affiliate earnings service. Accrual is produced solely by a scheduled reconciliation job at minute 15 of each hour that honours a thirty-minute grace window, so a creator's earning appears between thirty and ninety minutes after the sale, and never at all if that job is disabled or failing. The job's own javadoc still describes a synchronous call inside the redemption transaction that no longer exists, s
missed_by: Webhook tests assert the redemption row only; no test asserts an affiliate_earnings row exists after a redemption without running the job.

symptom: [Admin Dashboard / low Q35] The support stats DTO's average-response-time field is always zero because no first-reply timestamp column exists on support tickets to compute it from. Admins reading the stats panel see a real-looking zero rather than an absent metric.
missed_by: No assertion that reported stats fields are computed from stored data rather than constant defaults.

symptom: [Admin Dashboard / low Q35] The feature doc labels admin billing as mock-backed. In the current tree the list route runs a real paged specification query against the subscriptions repository, the metrics route counts by status and plan on the same repository, and the comp and override routes mutate real subscription rows with audit entries. Nothing returns hardcoded rows; the doc is wrong.
missed_by: Feature-status labels in the docs are not re-checked against the service implementations.

symptom: [Support Tickets / low Q33, 49] The feature doc claims the admin support escalate button hits a missing endpoint and that the support stats route 404s. Both routes exist: escalate is mapped on the admin support controller, requires a reason, raises priority to URGENT and audit-logs; stats is mapped on a sibling controller one path segment higher so it resolves as support/stats. The frontend contract posts to exactly those paths, so neither call 404s today.
missed_by: Feature docs are not diffed against the route inventory or the frontend API contract file.

symptom: [Brand Dashboard / low Q37] The brand layout registers its own window-level keydown listener for the command-bar chord and unconditionally opens the dialog, while the command bar registers a document-level listener that toggles it. The command bar only remains able to close itself because it stops propagation — remove or reorder that and the chord becomes open-only.
missed_by: No interaction test presses the chord twice and asserts the dialog closes.

symptom: [Brand Dashboard / low Q38] The feature doc claims there is no token auto-refresh and that a brand returning after a day idle is bounced to login. The client actually refreshes twice over: proactively when the decoded access-token expiry falls inside the skew window, and reactively once on a 401 before replaying the request, for as long as the thirty-day refresh cookie lives. The doc, not the code, is wrong.
missed_by: Feature docs are not re-validated against the API client's auth path.

symptom: [Brand Dashboard / high Q39] Campaign creation calls only the membership check, which resolves an active workspace member row and throws only when there is none; the role-restricting helper is never invoked on the create path, unlike update, publish and delete which pass explicit allowed-role lists. A workspace member with the VIEWER role can therefore create a campaign today. The frontend route guard reads the brand token and an onboarding flag but never inspects workspace role, so nothing stops it client-side either.
missed_by: No authorization test asserts a VIEWER is rejected on campaign create; role tests cover update/publish/delete only.

symptom: [Brand Dashboard / low Q40] The feature doc labels brand campaign detail as mock-backed. The page loader fires a real request to the campaign-by-id route alongside deals, analytics and the platform-fee lookup, and the backend declares that exact mapping. The analytics and fee calls are individually caught and degraded to null, which renders a thinner page on partial backend failure — probably what earned the mock label — but the page is live.
missed_by: Feature-status labels are inferred from degraded rendering rather than checked against the network calls.

symptom: [Creator Dashboard / low Q43] The feature doc claims creator affiliate earnings returns a 501 or shows a coming-soon placeholder. A real controller is mounted at the creator affiliate-earnings path, delegates to the earnings service with paging, the client calls exactly that path in live mode, and the page renders a dedicated view component. Rows are often empty, but that is data, not a stub.
missed_by: Feature docs are not re-checked against the controller and page implementations.

symptom: [Creator Dashboard / low Q45] The feature doc labels the creator wallet as mock surfaces. The wallet controller branches on the principal's user type on the summary, balance and transactions routes and calls user-scoped service methods for creators, with payouts creator-only; the creator wallet page's three routes all resolve. There is no brand-only filter stranding creators at zero.
missed_by: Feature-status labels are not re-validated against the controller's user-type branching.

symptom: [Support Tickets / medium Q47] Ticket status updates accept any parseable enum value with no transition graph — the service 400s only on an unparseable string and hands the value straight to the entity. The entity stamps resolvedAt when and only when the new value is RESOLVED and never clears it, so moving a ticket back out of RESOLVED leaves a stale resolved timestamp on an unresolved ticket, and re-setting RESOLVED restamps it. Only the audit entry's from/to metadata would ever reveal a nonsensical transition.
missed_by: No test drives an illegal status transition or asserts resolvedAt is cleared when a ticket reopens.

symptom: [Support Tickets / high Q48] No support ticket can be created anywhere in the application. There is no support controller outside the admin one, and that controller exposes only list, detail, reply, status update, assign and escalate — no create route for a user or for an admin. On the frontend the brand help page is static how-it-works copy whose only action funnels the user into the Meera chat with a preseeded prompt: no form, no contact address, no client call. A ticket can only come into existence by a direct database insert.
missed_by: Admin-side ticket tests seed rows directly into the database, so the absent creation path is never exercised.

symptom: [Support Tickets / low Q50] The admin support detail DTO exposes a relatedEntities field typed as a list of bare Object, but support_tickets has no campaign or collaboration column and no cross-reference table exists — the DTO's own javadoc says so. The field can never be populated, and the category column beside it is a free-text label rather than a foreign key, so admins must infer the related campaign from the subject and message thread.
missed_by: No check that every DTO field has a persistence source; the untyped List<Object> also defeats any schema-shape assertion.

symptom: [Escrow / low Q1] When an escrow hold is funded, the "Campaign is live!" creator notification is skipped silently if the hold has no resolvable collaboration. Funding still succeeds and the ledger posting is written, but the creator is never told the money is secured and nothing is logged as a failure.
missed_by: A notification test that funds a hold whose collaboration cannot be resolved and asserts either a notification or an explicit error.

symptom: [Escrow / low Q1] The contract gate that must pass before escrow can be funded only checks that both signature timestamp columns are non-null; it never checks the contract's enum status. A contract row whose status is anything other than ACTIVE but whose two timestamps happen to be set would pass the funding gate.
missed_by: A funding test with a contract that has both signature timestamps set but a non-ACTIVE status.

symptom: [Contracts & Milestones / medium Q3, 43] Every payment milestone in the system carries release_condition = ON_POSTED, because no service ever writes a different value: the only construction site is ContractService, whose builder chain ends at dueDate and never calls releaseCondition, and the milestone write DTO carries no condition field for a caller to supply. A contract whose milestones read "upon approval" or "upon delivery" stores that phrasing only in the free-text description; the machine-readable condition the release gate reads is uniformly ON_POSTED.
missed_by: A test that creates a contract with a non-default milestone release condition and asserts the persisted enum value.

symptom: [Escrow / medium Q3] The milestone release-condition gate (assertReleaseConditionSatisfied) is skipped entirely unless a cutover instant is configured, and that setting ships blank. On a default deployment, releasing escrow therefore checks only FUNDED status, the cancellation guard and the dispute guard — deliverable state is never consulted before money moves to the creator.
missed_by: A release test run against default configuration (no cutover instant) that asserts the deliverable-status gate actually fires.

symptom: [Wallet / low Q5, 8] The wallet escrow_balance column is mapped on the entity and set to zero at wallet creation, and then never written by any service — funding a hold moves only the balance column through the ledger. Any consumer that reads escrowBalance directly gets a permanent 0.00. The brand dashboard is unaffected only because it derives the locked figure as a live SUM over FUNDED holds instead.
missed_by: A reconciliation check comparing wallet.escrow_balance against the SUM of that workspace's FUNDED escrow holds.

symptom: [Wallet / low Q8] The feature doc says the brand wallet tile is labelled "Funds in Escrow". The shipped page labels it "Funds Secured". Documentation fix only; the value rendered is correct.
missed_by: A copy/label check comparing doc-quoted UI strings against the rendered component.

symptom: [Wallet / medium Q10] The daily creator withdrawal cap counts WITHDRAWAL rows in wallet_transactions for the current UTC day, not withdrawal attempts. A withdrawal that passes the count check but then fails before its ledger row is posted is never counted, so a creator whose attempts fail downstream can make more attempts in a day than the cap allows.
missed_by: A test that fails a withdrawal after the cap check but before the ledger post, then asserts the day's remaining attempt allowance.

symptom: [Escrow / medium Q4] Two disputes raised on the same collaboration derive ledger idempotency keys with different prefixes, so the ledger's uniqueness constraint cannot dedupe a second dispute settlement of the same escrow hold. The only thing preventing the hold being paid out twice is the post-lock FROZEN/status re-check inside the settlement transaction — there is no second line of defence.
missed_by: A test settling two separate disputes against the same collaboration and asserting the ledger idempotency constraint rejects the second settlement.

symptom: [Payouts / low Q13] A javadoc block inside PayoutService still states that no separate payouts table exists in this slice. It is contradicted by code roughly fifty lines below it that persists Payout rows, and by the V48__payouts.sql migration. This stale comment is the source of the feature doc's false claim that payouts are not persisted and the webhook handler is a no-op.
missed_by: A doc/comment audit cross-checking javadoc claims about missing tables against the migration set.

symptom: [Payouts / low Q15] The feature doc says creator bank-account routes are missing or unwired. They exist on the wallet controller as payout-methods (GET masked list, POST add, PUT promote-to-primary) and the creator wallet page calls all of them. Documentation fix only.
missed_by: A route-inventory check comparing doc-claimed missing endpoints against the actual controller mappings.

symptom: [Invoicing & GST / low Q18] The feature doc claims commission invoices always render IGST. The code compares the first two characters of the company GSTIN against the customer GSTIN and renders CGST+SGST at nine percent each when they match. The doc's claim happens to hold today only because the shipped default company GSTIN is a placeholder string that can never match a real state code.
missed_by: A PDF-render test with a company GSTIN sharing the customer's state code, asserting which tax lines appear.

symptom: [Invoicing & GST / medium Q20] creator_profiles.tax_registration_status is captured and stored (set to GST_REGISTERED when a GSTIN is supplied) but nothing on the invoicing path reads it. The Doc#2 creator service invoice copies the GSTIN onto the row yet never branches on registration status, and its PDF renderer emits only a service value plus the report-only TCS line — there is no CGST, SGST or IGST rendering code in that renderer at all. A GST-registered creator's Doc#2 is byte-for-byte identical to an unregistered creator's.
missed_by: A golden-file comparison of Doc#2 PDFs for a GST-registered vs an unregistered creator.

symptom: [Platform Fees / medium Q23] The brand-facing platform fee endpoint reads the global PlatformFeeConfig basis points and returns them with a hardcoded source label of GLOBAL_DEFAULT and a compile-time-constant copy string that says ten percent, regardless of the number beside it. The charge path (resolveBrandFeeBps) consults SubscriptionService and charges a Pro workspace 700 bps. A Pro brand is therefore quoted 1000 bps and ten percent while actually being charged seven percent at publish, and the copy string would also be wrong for a Free brand if an admin ever edited the global rate.
missed_by: A test asserting the fee returned by the read endpoint equals the fee actually posted at campaign publish for the same workspace.

symptom: [Authentication / medium Q32] creatorLogin loads the user row by case-insensitive email and, if the user type is not CREATOR, throws WRONG_USER_TYPE with a 403 before the password is ever compared. An unauthenticated caller can therefore probe the creator login endpoint to learn that a given email exists as a brand account on the other side of the product.
missed_by: An auth test asserting that a wrong-user-type email and a nonexistent email produce indistinguishable responses.

symptom: [Authentication / high Q33] The access token is written to and read from localStorage or sessionStorage depending on the remember-me flag, so it stays script-readable and is exposed to any XSS on the page. The HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite cookie hardening protects only the refresh token.
missed_by: A security review of client-side token storage; static checks and auth tests both pass with the token in web storage.

symptom: [Authentication / low Q33] The feature doc says silent token auto-refresh is not wired on the frontend. It is: the fetch wrapper detects a 401 on a request that carried an auth header, calls refresh with credentials so the HttpOnly cookie travels, stores the new access token and retries the original request once, deduping concurrent 401s per role. Documentation fix only.
missed_by: A doc audit against the fetch wrapper's 401 branch.

symptom: [Authentication / medium Q34] Refresh rotation revokes the presented token, so when two browser tabs on the same device race a refresh, the loser presents an already-revoked token and is logged out. The only thing preventing this is the frontend's per-role in-flight dedupe, which does not span tabs.
missed_by: A multi-tab (or two-client) test firing simultaneous refreshes with the same refresh token.

symptom: [Authentication / medium Q35] There is no admin MFA unlock endpoint — the only method that clears the failed-MFA counter is an entity method invoked on a successful code verification, which a locked-out admin cannot reach. Recovery is to wait out the configured cooldown (the lockout is an expiry instant, not a sticky flag), but the lockout response is indistinguishable from bad credentials, so the admin gets no signal that waiting is the remedy. A long-configured cooldown or a lost TOTP secret leaves only a direct database update.
missed_by: An admin-recovery walkthrough that locks an account out and tries to regain access using only shipped routes.

symptom: [Workspaces & Members / low Q38] The feature doc says the workspace phone field is dropped silently / is UI-only. The PATCH handler passes it into the update service, which format-checks it and calls updatePhone on the entity, backed by a real nullable phone column added by migration V20260718180000. It round-trips like billing email. Documentation fix only.
missed_by: A doc audit against the entity mapping and migration set.

symptom: [Billing & Subscriptions / low Q28] The feature doc claims the subscription.activated webhook has no route, so a paying brand never becomes ACTIVE. The single POST receive method has an explicit activated arm calling handleSubscriptionEvent inside a transaction, and six subscription event types are routed in total (activated, charged, halted, pending, cancelled, completed). Documentation fix only.
missed_by: A doc audit against the webhook controller's event switch.

symptom: [Billing & Subscriptions / low Q30] The feature doc claims there is no listener for subscription halted or payment-failed, so a workspace is never told a billing payment failed. Both after-commit async handlers exist and send billing emails to the resolved billing recipient. Documentation fix only (note the recipient is the resolved billing contact, not necessarily the OWNER).
missed_by: A doc audit against the notification listener's registered event handlers.

symptom: [Workspaces & Members / low Q40] The feature doc says workspace verification status is unmapped, unenforced and not surfaced. It is a non-null enum column defaulting to unverified, CampaignValidator refuses to set a campaign ACTIVE unless the workspace is VERIFIED, KYC submission moves it to PENDING via OnboardingService, admins decide it, and a dedicated frontend hook drives the KYC prompt from it. Documentation fix only.
missed_by: A doc audit against the entity column, validator and frontend hook.

symptom: [Contracts & Milestones / medium Q41] Contract PDF generation and R2 storage run after the contract is already ACTIVE and the whole block is best-effort — failures are swallowed so a storage problem cannot roll back a recorded signature. If R2 is unconfigured or the PUT fails, the contract stays ACTIVE with a null pdf_r2_key and the download endpoint 404s forever, with no retry, no marker and no signal to either party.
missed_by: A contract-signing test run with R2 unconfigured that then asserts the PDF download succeeds.

symptom: [Contracts & Milestones / medium Q42] The contract tamper hash is a SHA-256 over the request record's own toString() output, written into termsJson as a small JSON wrapper. The digest therefore depends on the Java record's field order and rendering rather than on a canonical document, so any refactor of that record's fields or formatting silently invalidates every previously stored hash and the hash cannot be independently recomputed from the contract as issued.
missed_by: A tamper-detection test that recomputes the hash from the persisted contract rather than from the original request object.

symptom: [Contracts & Milestones / medium Q44] Milestone amounts are validated exactly once, at contract generation, against the collaboration's agreed rate — only when that rate is non-null, and only as a not-to-exceed rather than an equality. The campaign budget is never compared at all, and the signature path performs no amount validation whatsoever. Editing the campaign budget afterwards in a different flow touches no contract row and fires no revalidation, so a 50,000-rupee contract can sit permanently attached to a 60,000-rupee campaign with no reconciliation anywhere.
missed_by: A test that changes a campaign budget after contract signature and asserts contract/campaign amount consistency.

symptom: [Contracts & Milestones / low Q45] The feature doc says no event is published after both contract signatures land, so the brand is never prompted to fund. ContractReadyForEscrowEvent is published from the prompt method that runs right after the second signature, and NotificationListener has an after-commit handler that sends a "Secure the funds to get started" notification to the resolved brand owner. Documentation fix only.
missed_by: A doc audit against the event publisher and its registered listener.

symptom: [Contracts & Milestones / medium Q45] The publish of ContractReadyForEscrowEvent after the second contract signature is wrapped in a catch that logs and swallows. If the brand owner cannot be resolved, the signature still succeeds and the contract goes ACTIVE but the brand is never prompted to secure the funds, with no visible failure. (The prompt is also skipped by design when the collaboration already has a FUNDED hold.)
missed_by: A signing test in which brand-owner resolution fails, asserting either a notification or a surfaced error.

symptom: [Disputes / low Q48] DisputeStatus.UNDER_REVIEW can never be reached. The entity has a guarded markUnderReview() transition, but it has zero callers anywhere in the service or web layers, and the admin dispute controller exposes only list and resolve. The value is live only as a read-side predicate (it is included in every active-dispute set), which makes a grep for the constant look busier than the behaviour is — no dispute is ever actually placed under review.
missed_by: A caller-count check on entity transition methods, or a state-machine test asserting every enum value is reachable.

symptom: [Disputes / medium Q50] There is no admin dispute detail endpoint — the controller exposes only a list and a resolve-by-id. The richer record (reason, resolution notes, resolver, timestamps) is returned only as the response to the resolve call, so an admin decides how to split disputed escrow money while seeing nothing but the summary row from the list. The admin UI documents the gap in its own component header rather than faking it.
missed_by: An admin-workflow test that opens a dispute and asserts the reason text is readable before resolving it.

symptom: [Uploads & Storage / low Q53] The feature doc makes two stale claims: that no generic uploads route exists, and that the frontend upload module is still a mock returning a fabricated R2 URL. Both are fixed — UploadController has a POST multipart handler delegating to UploadService, and src/lib/upload.ts goes through the real uploads client. The generic route serves profile and logo assets while deliverables use their own multipart route; neither is dead. Documentation fix only.
missed_by: A doc audit against the controller mappings and the frontend upload module.

symptom: [Uploads & Storage / medium Q54] The deliverable cleanup job can only delete R2 keys it reads back out of the deliverable's files_json column, but that column is overwritten on every new upload and holds only the current version's keys — so per-version cleanup finds nothing to delete and superseded R2 objects are never reclaimed. The job's own javadoc records this, and it defaults to dry-run on top of that.
missed_by: A test that uploads two versions of a deliverable, runs the cleanup job, and asserts the superseded object is gone from R2.

symptom: [Uploads & Storage / low Q55] R2StorageService.presignPut builds a real presigned PUT URL but has no callers outside its own class. Direct-to-R2 client upload is not partially built — it is entirely unimplemented above the storage layer: no request DTO, no route, no client call, and no server-side completion step to record the key after a client-side PUT. Every upload in the product streams through the backend instead.
missed_by: A dead-code / unused-public-method sweep across the storage integration layer.

symptom: [Campaigns / medium Q3] A DIRECT-type campaign requires a connected store, and the backend rejects the DRAFT save with a NO_STORE_INTEGRATION 409 at create time. The new-campaign form has no reference to store-integration state at all, so a brand picks the DIRECT type, fills the whole form, and only learns the requirement as a server error on submit.
missed_by: a frontend test that picks the DIRECT campaign type with no store connected and asserts an inline precondition warning before submit

symptom: [Campaigns / low Q3] The feature doc says a DIRECT campaign's store-integration requirement surfaces at publish time (or is ungated). The code gates it in CampaignService.create, before the DRAFT row is ever built, and update has no equivalent check — so the doc names the wrong edge.
missed_by: a doc-vs-code review of where requiresStoreIntegration is actually called

symptom: [Campaigns / medium Q4] The brand publish fee is charged on every DRAFT-to-ACTIVE transition, but the ledger idempotency key is scoped to the campaign alone ('brand-fee-publish:<campaign>'). A pause-then-republish cycle re-enters chargeOnPublish and the second charge is silently suppressed by the duplicate key instead of either re-billing or being explicitly declined — no error, no log the operator acts on.
missed_by: a test that publishes, pauses, and republishes one campaign and asserts the intended number of fee postings

symptom: [Collaborations & Deals / medium Q6, 36] Application-created (and every other workspace-scoped) notification resolves a single recipient via findFirstByWorkspaceIdAndRoleAndActiveTrue — the first ACTIVE OWNER. An ADMIN or MANAGER in the same workspace never gets the in-app row or the email, so their notification bell stays empty when a creator applies.
missed_by: a test with a workspace holding an OWNER plus a non-owner ADMIN that asserts notification rows for both

symptom: [Collaborations & Deals / medium Q6] The brand deal dashboard loads the deal list once in a mount effect — no interval, no list-level SSE. The only stream it opens is the message stream for an already-selected deal, so a brand sitting on the page never sees a newly arrived application until they manually reload.
missed_by: an E2E test that keeps the deal dashboard open while a creator applies and asserts the new deal appears without a reload

symptom: [Collaborations & Deals / low Q8] The deal response now carries real deliverablesTotal and deliverablesDone counts, but the brand deal-room list maps only the total into its deliverables field. deliverablesDone is never read anywhere in the brand dashboard, so no progress ('2 of 5 done') is shown despite the backend computing it.
missed_by: a render test asserting the deal card shows completed-vs-total deliverables

missed_by: a doc-vs-code review of toDealResponse

The code documents this as a known residual.
missed_by: a test that commits a collaboration with a null agreed rate and then accepts an offer that should breach budgetMax

It is rejected only later at accept, with AMOUNT_EXCEEDS_BUDGET.
missed_by: a test countering above budgetMax and asserting rejection at counter time

symptom: [Deliverables / medium Q12] A YouTube post URL is recognised and routed to a FALLBACK_YOUTUBE_UNSUPPORTED outcome because no YouTube client exists. That outcome is never persisted — no column on the deliverable, no verification-attempt table, no metric — only a WARN log and an in-memory tally in the sweep job's final info line. The deliverable keeps its creator-reported numbers and is re-swept and re-logged every six hours forever, with nobody notified that verification is impossible.
missed_by: a test asserting a verification attempt leaves a persisted outcome the UI or an operator can read

symptom: [Deliverables / medium Q13] When a deliverable metric row already has source PLATFORM_VERIFIED, applyReport skips the three number assignments but still writes link, proof screenshot key, reporting creator id and reportedAt. The submit path does no source check, so a creator reporting 50000 views over a platform-verified 5000 gets a 200 with the untouched 5000 echoed back — no error and no indication their numbers were discarded.
missed_by: a test posting a creator metric report against a PLATFORM_VERIFIED row and asserting a rejection rather than a 200 echo

symptom: [Deliverables / high Q14] Deliverable carries no JPA @Version and the brand review path loads it through a plain findByIdAndWorkspaceId with no pessimistic lock. Two brand members approving the same SUBMITTED deliverable in parallel both read SUBMITTED, both pass canReview, and both enter the escrow release attempt — only EscrowService's own locking and idempotency stands between that and a double payout.
